content.title: NCAA tournament takeaways: Final Four-bound Arizona looks like the favorite; can Texas, South Carolina women be stopped?
content.text: A pair of Final Four spots were on the line Saturday in the men’s tournament, and the two games didn’t disappoint.Arizona made it to the Final Four for the first time in 25 years after a convincing win over Purdue, while Illinois ended Iowa’s NCAA tournament run. The final two spots will be decided on Sunday to wrap up the second weekend.AdvertisementThe women’s Elite Eight field is set now, too, after a day of blowout wins that set up what should be a great regional final round.Here are the highlights from Saturday’s NCAA tournament action:Arizona punches Final Four ticket; is it the favorite?Duke entered the NCAA tournament as the No. 1 overall seed. But through four games of NCAA tournament play, Arizona looks like the favorite to cut down the nets in Indianapolis.The Wildcats received their first challenge of the tournament on Saturday as No. 2 seed Purdue took a 38-31 lead into halftime. That challenge lasted precisely 20 minutes.Arizona dominated the second half to the tune of a 48-26 advantage and a 79-64 runaway win to advance to the Final Four. Head coach Tommy Lloyd made the necessary second-half adjustments, and Arizona’s superior talent prevailed on the floor.AdvertisementAll-Big 12 freshman Koa Peat led four starters in double figures with 20 points, 7 rebounds and 3 assists. As a team, the Wildcats were efficient (79 points on 58 shots) and surgical with the ball (15 assists, 6 turnovers).Purdue’s All-America leader Braden Smith started the game shooting 3 of 4 from the field. He went 1 for 11 the rest of the way. And a Purdue unit that ranked second in the nation in KenPom’s adjusted offensive efficiency was no match for Arizona’s top-ranked defense that limited the Boilermakers to 38% shooting from the field.Before Saturday, nobody in the tournament had tested the Wildcats. In the first three rounds, Arizona cruised to 34-, 12- and 21-point wins over Long Island, Utah State and Arkansas, respectively. Arizona dropped 109 points on No. 4 seed Arkansas in Thursday’s Sweet 16 win.AdvertisementDuke and Michigan — if they advance on Sunday — will certainly have something to say about it. But from here, Arizona looks like the team to beat in Indianapolis.-Jason OwensIllinois gets past Iowa, horn delay to reach Final FourIt took them a bit to shut No. 9 Iowa down, but the Illini are headed to their first Final Four in more than two decades.Illinois pulled away late to grab a 71-59 win over the Hawkeyes in the first Elite Eight matchup of the night on Saturday. That secured the school’s first trip to the Final Four since 2005, the same year they fell to North Carolina in the national championship game.AdvertisementWhile Iowa led for the entire first half and hung in for a battle for much of the second half, the Hawkeyes hit a wall late. They made just one of their final 13 shots and completely shut down offensively. Illinois, meanwhile, made seven of its last nine. The Hawkeyes, who knocked off top-seeded Florida in the second round, were playing in their first Elite Eight since 1987 under first year coach Ben McCollum.While the game ended up finishing normally, there was one of the strangest delays in NCAA tournament history in the first half. The contest was paused for about 11 minutes after the buzzer inside the Toyota Center wouldn’t shut off. That left fans inside the Houston arena incredibly annoyed, and led to both teams starting warm-up drills while officials tried to get it fixed. Eventually, they just used an air horn the rest of the way."Surely there's a way to unplug this -- surely there's a horn expert somewhere in this building!" Kevin Harlan on the call as an issue with the horn gets worked on. pic.twitter.com/dnI0W9HOWT— CBS Sports College Basketball 🏀 (@CBSSportsCBB) March 28, 2026Illinois has now won all four of its NCAA tournament games by double digits. While it let Iowa hang around for longer than many may have expected, the Illini look very capable of securing what would not only be their first ever national championship, but the Big Ten’s first national title since 2000.Advertisement-Ryan YoungCan Miles, Suarez lead TCU to challenge South Carolina?Olivia Miles and Marta Suarez did it all for No. 3 seed TCU in a win over 10 seed Virginia in the women’s bracket, combining for 61 of the Horned Frogs’ 79 points.They’ll need all that and more to challenge top-seeded South Carolina in Monday’s Sacramento 4 regional final.Suarez posted a career-high 33 points alongside 10 rebounds while shooting 4 of 7 from 3. Miles flirted with a triple-double with 28 points, 10 rebounds, 7 assists and 2 steals. She shot 11 of 14 from the field. The backcourt duo paced a rally from a 36-35 halftime deficit to a 79-69 win.South Carolina, meanwhile, overwhelmed No. 4 seed Oklahoma. The Gamecocks opened the game with a 10-0 run and were never challenged in a 94-68 win.AdvertisementSouth Carolina also rode its backcourt to victory as Ta'Niya Latson tallied 28 points and five assists while hitting all four of her 3-point attempts and each of her 10 free throws. Raven Johnson added 18 points and three assists while shooting 8 of 11 from the field.South Carolina was very much the dominant team on Saturday that tallied a 33-3 record before Saturday’s tip. Anything short of TCU’s absolute best won’t stand a chance of an upset on Monday.-Jason OwensMichigan rolls to Elite Eight, has to find a way past No. 1 Texas on the roadThe Michigan women, like the men did the day before, cruised into the Elite Eight to open the day on Sunday with yet another dominant win.AdvertisementThe Wolverines, behind 19 points from Olivia Olson, beat Louisville 71-52. It marked their third straight double-digit blowout win so far this tournament, though remarkably it was their closest game yet. Monday’s contest in Fort Worth, however, should be anything but.The Wolverines will have to match up with top-seeded Texas in what will essentially be a road game. The Longhorns have been on an equally dominant run so far this postseason, and they are fresh off a 22-point win over Kentucky in the Sweet 16. They jumped out to a 29-11 start in the first quarter, and Madison Booker and Jordan Lee combined for 35 points.“They were on a different planet today, especially that first quarter,” Kentucky coach Kenny Brooks said of Texas. “They came out and they were aggressive. They play right to the rules. … They have to be the favorite or one of the favorites. I haven’t had a chance to see UConn play this year, but I know that Texas is playing on a different level right now.”Texas is headed to the Elite Eight after a dominant win over Kentucky on Saturday. (AP/LM Otero) (ASSOCIATED PRESS)Texas is seeking a return trip to the Final Four this season after it was knocked out by South Carolina in the semifinals last spring. The Longhorns haven’t won a national title since 1986.AdvertisementThey’ve got a big advantage, too, after winning the SEC tournament championship game. Monday’s game will take place just shy of 200 miles away from Texas’ campus in Austin. It’s sure to feel like a home game for the Longhorns once again.There’s little doubt that Monday’s contest will be a tough battle. Both teams are playing incredible basketball so far this March.But if Michigan is going to reach its first-ever Final Four, it’ll have to find a way to knock off Booker and Texas — and, now on an 11-game win streak, they seem just about unstoppable.-Ryan YoungJosh Heim/Yahoo Sports (Yahoo Sports)Here’s how everything played out on Saturday:AdvertisementMarch Madness men’s Elite Eight resultsMarch Madness women’s Sweet 16 resultsLive coverage is over101 updatesSat, March 28, 2026 at 7:03 PM UTCYahoo Sports StaffSun, March 29, 2026 at 3:08 AM UTCYahoo Sports StaffThe Wildcats just proved to be too much in the second half of this one and sprinted away with the win.Koa Peat led the way with 20 points, but four Wildcats had 14 or more points in the win.
